pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which action shows attentive listening? (1 mark)
   A. Looking out of the window
   B. Looking at the speaker and staying quiet
   C. Talking to a friend
   D. Drawing on your desk

2. Plural means (1 mark)
   A. only one
   B. nothing
   C. the biggest
   D. more than one

3. In the passage: Ugali is made from maize flour, what is ugali made from? (1 mark)
   A. millet
   B. wheat only
   C. rice
   D. maize flour

4. What should you do if you make a mistake in your exercise book? (1 mark)
   A. Scribble over it hard
   B. Blame a friend
   C. Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   D. Tear the page

5. Which letter hangs below the base line in English handwriting? (1 mark)
   A. g
   B. c
   C. a
   D. o

6. A verb is (1 mark)
   A. a word that shows an action
   B. a word that names a person
   C. a word that describes a colour
   D. a joining word

7. What should you do if you did not hear a question? (1 mark)
   A. Guess loudly
   B. Laugh
   C. Leave
   D. Politely ask for it to be repeated

8. What is a resource person? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of book
   B. A pupil who is late
   C. A bag for books
   D. A person with special knowledge who visits to teach

9. In a written dialogue the speaker's name usually comes (1 mark)
   A. in the middle of a word
   B. at the start of the line
   C. on a different page
   D. at the end

10. What should you do when you use a simile or metaphor? (1 mark)
   A. Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   B. Use very many in one sentence
   C. Never explain it
   D. Use hurtful comparisons

11. What is a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. A choir
   B. A group that meets to share and discuss books
   C. A team for running
   D. A group that sells books

12. What is the setting of a story? (1 mark)
   A. Where and when it happens
   B. The price
   C. The name of the writer
   D. The last line

13. Which question helps you plan an experience to tell? (1 mark)
   A. Where is the moon?
   B. How long is the ruler?
   C. Who was there?
   D. What colour is the wall?

14. Which of these should you include when describing an event? (1 mark)
   A. Only the date
   B. Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   C. Nothing
   D. Only the name

15. A seller buys mangoes for 300 shillings and sells them for 450 shillings. What is the profit? (1 mark)
   A. 150 shillings
   B. 300 shillings
   C. 450 shillings
   D. 750 shillings

16. What is scanning? (1 mark)
   A. Looking quickly for a specific piece of information
   B. Singing
   C. Writing a story
   D. Reading for the main idea only

17. What is a customer? (1 mark)
   A. A person who buys
   B. A person who sells only
   C. A kind of shop
   D. A type of money

18. What does it mean to advocate for animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. To hide them
   B. To ignore them
   C. To speak in support of caring for animals
   D. To harm animals

19. What is a refrain? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. A line that is repeated
   C. A page
   D. A rhyme only

20. What does rhyme mean? (1 mark)
   A. Words with capital letters
   B. Words with no vowels
   C. Words with the same ending sound
   D. Words with many letters

21. Which question helps you find ideas from a picture? (1 mark)
   A. Who is in the picture?
   B. Who printed it?
   C. What page is this?
   D. How heavy is the paper?

22. Which element tells where and when a story happens? (1 mark)
   A. Ending
   B. Title
   C. Character
   D. Setting

23. Which interjection shows disgust? (1 mark)
   A. Aha
   B. Hurray
   C. Bravo
   D. Yuck

24. Which punctuation mark often follows an interjection showing strong feeling? (1 mark)
   A. Full stop
   B. Colon
   C. Question mark
   D. Exclamation mark

25. How should you read an interjection aloud? (1 mark)
   A. In a flat voice
   B. Without pausing
   C. With the feeling it shows
   D. Very quietly always

26. What is role play? (1 mark)
   A. Reading silently
   B. Acting out a situation
   C. Drawing only
   D. Copying

27. What should you do first when a call is answered? (1 mark)
   A. Ask for money
   B. Shout
   C. Hang up
   D. Greet politely

28. Which field asks how old you are? (1 mark)
   A. Class
   B. School
   C. Age
   D. Signature

29. Why is it important to obey leaders? (1 mark)
   A. It is a game
   B. It is boring
   C. It keeps order, peace and safety
   D. It makes noise

30. Which two words in the poem Lead with honesty rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. fair and strong
   B. poem and song
   C. all and call
   D. leader and rule

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain how the meaning of You are coming to school changes when it is a statement and when it is a question. (3 marks)

32. Name three parts of a simple form. (3 marks)

33. Describe how to mark a line of a poem for reading aloud. (4 marks)

34. Compose a four-line poem about a good leader. Make lines two and four rhyme. (4 marks)

35. Write a four-line dialogue between two friends deciding what to do in their free time. Use two interjections. (4 marks)

36. State three benefits of reading widely. (3 marks)

37. Describe the steps in writing a story from a picture. (4 marks)

38. Explain what attentive listening means. (2 marks)

39. Write two sentences using the interjections Hurray and Ouch. (2 marks)

40. Explain what to do when you get a small burn and why. (4 marks)

41. Write a five-line role play dialogue on personal safety between a child and a stranger. Show the speaker names and use question marks correctly. (5 marks)

42. Join the sentences with when: I counted my money. The bell rang. (2 marks)

43. List three steps for understanding a poem. (3 marks)

44. Write three instructions for what to do when it starts to rain at school. Use first, then and finally. (4 marks)

45. Explain why clear instructions are important on a road. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Looking at the speaker and staying quiet
   Attentive listening means giving your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker.

2. D — more than one
   Plural nouns name two or more.

3. D — maize flour
   The passage states that ugali is made from maize flour.

4. C — Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   Neat correction keeps the page clean.

5. A — g
   The letter g has a tail that goes below the line.

6. A — a word that shows an action
   Verbs show what is done.

7. D — Politely ask for it to be repeated
   Asking politely helps you answer correctly.

8. D — A person with special knowledge who visits to teach
   A nurse visiting a class is an example of a resource person.

9. B — at the start of the line
   The name shows who speaks.

10. A — Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   Clear and kind comparisons work best.

11. B — A group that meets to share and discuss books
   A reading club shares books and reading.

12. A — Where and when it happens
   Setting means place and time.

13. C — Who was there?
   Who, what, where, when, why and how help plan a story.

14. B — Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   These details make the event clear.

15. A — 150 shillings
   450 minus 300 is 150.

16. A — Looking quickly for a specific piece of information
   Scanning searches for a detail.

17. A — A person who buys
   A customer buys goods or services.

18. C — To speak in support of caring for animals
   Advocating means speaking in support.

19. B — A line that is repeated
   A refrain is repeated in a poem or song.

20. C — Words with the same ending sound
   Rhyming words sound alike at the end.

21. A — Who is in the picture?
   Who, where, what and why give story ideas.

22. D — Setting
   Setting means place and time.

23. D — Yuck
   Yuck shows disgust.

24. D — Exclamation mark
   Exclamation marks show strong feeling.

25. C — With the feeling it shows
   Intonation shows feeling.

26. B — Acting out a situation
   Role play acts a scene.

27. D — Greet politely
   A greeting begins the call.

28. C — Age
   Age records how old you are.

29. C — It keeps order, peace and safety
   Obeying fair leaders keeps everyone safe.

30. C — all and call
   All and call have the same ending sound.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: As a statement the voice falls and it tells something. As a question the voice rises and it asks something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the two meanings and one mark for the voice movement.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, instructions, fields, signature, date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Underline words to stress, draw a slash where you will pause, read the line using your marks and check that it sounds natural.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on leadership with two rhyming lines, for example A good leader listens, Speaks the truth each day, Helps the weak and lonely, And shows the proper way.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme and four lines, two marks for rhyme.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines with speaker names, colons, a clear topic and two suitable interjections.
   Working / marking points: One mark for names and colons, one mark for suitable content, one mark for each interjection.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary, improves spelling, gives new ideas, makes you a better writer and speaker, gives enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each benefit.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Look at the whole picture, ask who where and what, plan the characters, setting, problem and ending, write the story in order, and check it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attentive listening means choosing to give your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker so that you understand and remember what is said.
   Working / marking points: One mark for choosing to pay attention and one mark for understanding or remembering.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hurray! We won the match. Ouch! I hurt my foot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water for several minutes to reduce pain, cover it with a clean cloth and tell an adult or go to a clinic.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for cool water, the reason, clean cover and telling an adult.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five correct lines, for example Child: Good afternoon. Stranger: Do you want a ride? Child: No, thank you. I will wait for my mother. Stranger: Are you sure? Child: Yes, I am telling my teacher.
   Working / marking points: One mark for speaker names, one for a safe message, one for correct questions and two for five clear lines.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: When I counted my money, the bell rang.
   Working / marking points: One mark for using when and one mark for the comma.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read it aloud more than once, find meanings of new words, say the message in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, go into the classroom. Then close the windows. Finally, wait for the rain to stop.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for using all three signal words.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear road instructions and signs tell drivers and walkers what to do, which prevents accidents and keeps everyone safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for telling what to do, one for preventing accidents, one for safety.
